messages:
sasha: Bringing up halley13b (13B) int4 canary — hitting intermittent OOMs under bursty multi-user traffic. Suspect mem fragmentation + aggressive max_new_tokens defaults. Posting quick logs and perf numbers.

maya: can you paste the exact OOM log? also what backend (vpc/dedicated/hosted)?

sasha: hosted canary (dedicated pool small). log snippet: ```
[2026-02-18 13:02:45] ERROR runtime: allocation failed: CUDA out of memory (requested 1.2GB)
stack: serve/runtime/kv_cache.go:142 evictSlots
serve/runtime/generation.go:88 allocateKV
```
seems to spike after ~3 large requests in parallel (each max_new_tokens=512).

liam: sounds like two levers: reduce per-request max_new_tokens default and tighten batching window / max_batch_size so the memory working-set doesn't spike. also enabling more aggressive KV eviction might help.

nina: quant results: int4 gives ~35% lower p99 latency, but evals show a small quality drop — ~0.8% BLEU and a handful of prompt failures on long-context summarization. tradeoff looks reasonable if we avoid OOMs.

maya: can we reproduce locally with a synthetic load? i can run a 50qps burst test against canary with the same prompt set.

sasha: yes please. i also tried a quick tweak: set default_max_new_tokens=256 and max_batch_size=6 — reduced OOMs but still saw 1 crash in 10k requests.

liam: try these changes for the canary config: 
```json
{
  "default_max_new_tokens": "256",
  "max_batch_size": "4",
  "batch_window_ms": "8",
  "kv_eviction_policy": "aggressive",
  "slot_compactor_interval_s": "60",
  "enable_prefix_warmup": "true"
}
```
that reduces peak allocations and forces more frequent compaction.

nina: add an inline fallback rule: if OOM rate > 0.1% in canary, route to halley13b-int8 variant. we should also include a quality gate comparing sacreBLEU on a short eval set before promoting.

sasha: good call. will push the config to canary. maya — can you run the 50qps burst with both the old and new configs and capture p50/p95/p99, OOM count, and sacreBLEU on our long-context summarization eval?

maya: on it. starting tests now.

eng-ml-bot: Deploy started: canary config update for model=halley13b-int4 by sasha. Rollout: 5% traffic -> 20% over 30m if no errors.

maya: quick preliminary: with new config (max_new_tokens=256, batch_size=4): p99 dropped 28%, OOMs -> 0 in 20k requests. sacreBLEU dropped 0.9 vs baseline int8. latency improvement still solid. full results in ~10m.

liam: that's promising. if OOMs are gone and quality delta ~1% we can keep int4 as default for hosted but enable int8 fallback via routing policy and add a note in model catalog about the quality delta and recommendations for long-context summarization.

nina: for Dedicated customers we should expose a toggle for "quality-first" vs "cost-first" quant preference so teams can choose int8 by default if they care about fidelity.

sasha: action items:
- sasha: push canary config (done) and monitor for 1h after promotion
- maya: upload full perf/eval CSVs to the model onboarding doc and link in the ticket
- liam: add fallback routing rule + adjust rollout policy in deployment config
- nina: draft catalog note (quant tradeoffs + recommended max_new_tokens defaults)

maya: attaching short perf summary: p50 42ms -> 31ms, p95 120ms -> 85ms, p99 340ms -> 245ms, OOMs 7 -> 0 (20k requests). sacreBLEU: 33.8 -> 32.9.

sasha: thanks. going to run a longer 100k request soak overnight with the new config and the KV compactor enabled. will update tomorrow. :thumbsup:

liam: if soak looks stable we can schedule a gradual rollout to 50% tomorrow and set alerting for any OOM spikes or sacreBLEU regression >1.2%.

nina: also add an eval that exercises long token generations ( >350 tokens) in the canary gating — those were where we saw most prompt failures.

sasha: noted. closing the immediate OOM triage — followups tracked in #model-onboard-1742.

maya: ack. thanks team. :rocket:
